A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIST2Loss work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on regression, visual grounding, robotic manipulation, reward modeling, and image generation, plus ablations and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains these original results and adds RealWorldQA retention and visual-grounding failure analyses in Tables 7 and 13.

M1.justification: The distance-induced targets, combined cross-entropy/KL objective, and Appendix A workarounds are retained. v5 clarifies independent component losses and temperature selection without establishing a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: v5 adds RealWorldQA evaluation of the model fine-tuned for RefCOCO grounding (Appendix C.2, Table 7). Existing training and evaluation datasets and tasks remain; the shared-failure RefCOCO analysis selects examples within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged, including Ferretv2, both Florence-2 sizes, RT-2, and the reward-model and image-generation baselines. New analyses use backbone or SFT controls. Newly discussed methods such as NTIL are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces mean IoU evaluation on RefCOCO testA examples where both models have IoU below 0.5. v5 also adds the RealWorldQA retention evaluation. Existing experimental settings remain; explicit temperature values are newly disclosed rather than demonstrated setting changes.

E4.justification: Table 7 extends the existing catastrophic-forgetting analysis from reward modeling/MMLU to visual grounding/RealWorldQA. Appendix F and Table 13 add quantitative geometric-error analysis on shared failures. Earlier ablations, metric sanity checks, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeds for regression, ten for the Table 5 ablation, and means and standard deviations in Tables 5 and 11. Both acknowledge limited repeated runs elsewhere. The new analyses introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing result values are retained. New entries report RealWorldQA accuracy of 54.4 for the backbone and 54.3 after DIST2Loss grounding fine-tuning, and shared-failure IoU of 31.0 for SFT versus 40.3 for DIST2Loss. These are additional analyses, not revised original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds mathematical reasoning for temperature calibration using the digit Gaussian kernel and target entropy relative to log K; v3 provides only qualitative temperature guidance. The original loss equations and policy-optimization result remain. The added entropy argument does not provide a complete derivation.

C1.justification: The rewritten abstract foregrounds the entropy-regularized reinforcement-learning interpretation, but this already appears in v3's introduction, Section 2.3, and conclusion. The central claims about distance-aware supervision, architectural compatibility, and data efficiency retain their scope.

C2.justification: v5 interprets shared grounding failures as evidence of better geometric alignment and extends its preservation-of-unrelated-abilities interpretation to visual question answering. Existing credit-assignment and asymptotic limitations remain. The conclusion adds specific future directions involving multitask training and non-metric outputs.

D1.justification: v5 explicitly gives temperature 1 for digits and approximately 9.7 for a 16,384-entry VQ codebook, alongside component-wise loss details. Conversely, its reproducibility statement removes promises to release code, full configurations, outputs, and scripts. This does not establish that previously available resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands the brief loss-function discussion into loss-based, module-based, and target-based approaches. Seven added works support explicit distinctions from ordinal losses, attention priors, similarity-based smoothing, knowledge distillation, and NTIL, materially strengthening comparison with closely related research.

P1.justification: v5 rewrites the abstract, expands Section 2.2, revises related-work prose and the conclusion, and corrects affiliations and terminology. It adds acknowledgements and removes the LLM-usage disclosure. The principal section order and most method and experimental prose remain.

P2.justification: v5 adds Table 13, expands Table 7, restyles and compresses several tables, and rearranges appendix displays. Table 11 becomes substantially denser. Existing prompt and qualitative figures are relocated and renumbered; the main diagrams and qualitative imagery are retained.

improvement.justification: The new forgetting and shared-failure analyses (Tables 7 and 13) provide targeted support absent from v3, while Section 4 better distinguishes neighboring methods. Explicit temperatures improve implementation disclosure. These gains are limited by incomplete entropy-calibration reasoning, removal of release commitments, and denser tables. The core method and original benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
